title: All strength is His, so you never face anything alone
subtitle: Al-Qawiyy: the All-Strong, source of every power you have
intro: Al-Qawiyy (الْقَوِيُّ) means The All-Strong: Allah has perfect, unlimited strength that never weakens, never tires and always accomplishes what He intends. Every ounce of strength in creation is borrowed from Him. Knowing this name turns la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah from a phrase into a source of real courage.

root.sense: Quwwa is strength: the capacity to carry out what you intend. The Arabs called someone qawiyy when they had more than ordinary strength in body, mind or means. Its opposite, da'if, is the one who wants to lift the load but cannot. Al-Qawiyy is the One whose every intention is carried out, with no gap between willing and doing.

row.title: My tools make me strong
sub: money, contacts, the stick in my hand

row.title: He makes the tool work
sub: the stick split the sea by Him

knowing: Strength, in Arabic, is the ability to do what you intend. Humans always have a gap: we intend to lift the furniture, finish the project, quit the habit, and fall short. {idea}Al-Qawiyy has no gap. Whatever He intends is done, fully, without effort, fatigue or help{/idea}. His strength is not like physical strength; it is not built up, does not decline, and has no ceiling.

Every strength in creation comes from Him. The Quran praises some creatures for strength: Jibril is described as mighty in power, and the woman of Madyan recommended Musa as strong and trustworthy. The Prophet ﷺ said, as reported in Sahih Muslim, that the strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, while there is good in both. Strength is a gift. {trap}It becomes a trap only when we forget whose it is.{/trap}

Al-Qawiyy is almost always paired in the Quran with Al-Aziz (22:40, 22:74, 42:19, 58:21). Al-Qawiyy is the strength itself; Al-Aziz is the invincibility and honor that strength brings. Al-Matin, a close name, adds that this strength is firm and unwavering, never slackening.
seeing: The Quran gives a humbling test. Everything people call on besides Allah could never create a fly, even if they all gathered for it, and if a fly snatched something from them they could not take it back. Weak are the seeker and the sought. They have not valued Allah as He deserves; Allah is All-Strong, Almighty (22:73-74). In our age the lesson came as a virus invisible to the eye, and the most advanced nations shut their doors.

The prophets lived this name. Lut, surrounded by a mob, cried out that he wished he had strength or a strong support (11:80), and Al-Qawiyy answered for him. Musa reached the sea with an army behind him and said: no, my Lord is with me, He will guide me (26:62). A shepherd's stick split the sea, not because of the stick but because of the One behind it.
trusting: The Prophet ﷺ called la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah, there is no power and no strength except through Allah, a treasure from the treasures of Paradise (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). {reward}Say it before the job interview, the hard conversation, the hospital appointment, the exam: you are plugging into strength that does not run out.{/reward}

This does not make you passive. You still train, study and plan; the strong believer is beloved. But {idea}your confidence rests on Al-Qawiyy, not on the tools{/idea}, so losing a tool does not destroy you. Weakness also becomes a door: the moment you admit you cannot, you are finally asking the One who can.
loving: Children feel safe beside a strong parent. Believers feel safe beside Al-Qawiyy, whose strength is never used to bully, always to protect, provide and uphold justice. {reward}The heart loves Him because His limitless strength is on the side of the weak who turn to Him.{/reward}
now: You are about to walk into a meeting where you know you will be outnumbered and talked over. Your hands are cold. {idea}Whisper la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah, slowly, meaning every word.{/idea} Then walk in: your strength in that room is borrowed from Al-Qawiyy, and He does not lend weakly.
old: I am only as strong as my skills, my money and the people backing me.
new: All strength belongs to Al-Qawiyy; I use the means, but my confidence rests on Him.
try: Say la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah before each difficult task today, and notice how it changes the way you start.

dua.text: Ya Qawiyy, there is no power and no strength except through You. Strengthen my body for Your obedience, my heart against fear, and my faith against doubt, and never leave me to my own weakness.
dua.note: Call on Al-Qawiyy whenever you feel outmatched, together with la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah, which the Prophet ﷺ called a treasure of Paradise.

pairs.why: Their constant Quranic pairing: Al-Qawiyy is strength itself, Al-Aziz the invincibility and honor it brings.
Al-Qawiyy is perfect strength; Al-Matin is its firmness, a strength that never slackens or wavers (51:58).
In 42:19 He is Subtle with His servants and the All-Strong: unlimited strength used with gentle care.

faq.a: Al-Qawiyy means The All-Strong. It describes Allah as having perfect, unlimited strength that never weakens or tires and always accomplishes whatever He intends. All strength in creation is a gift from Him.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Qawiyy and Al-Matin?
faq.a: Al-Qawiyy describes the completeness of Allah's strength. Al-Matin describes its firmness and steadiness: a strength so intense and unwavering that it never slackens or needs rest. The two appear together in 51:58: the Possessor of strength, the Firm.

faq.q: What does la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah mean?
faq.a: It means there is no power and no strength except through Allah. It declares that every ability to do good or avoid harm comes from Al-Qawiyy. The Prophet ﷺ called it a treasure from the treasures of Paradise, as reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.

faq.q: Is it good for a Muslim to be strong?
faq.a: Yes. The Prophet ﷺ said the strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, while there is good in both (Sahih Muslim). Strength of body, mind and resolve is a gift to be used for good, without forgetting that it comes from Allah.
